BEAM/erl.exe making first-time outbound public network connection (post-RCE C2/exfil) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts for the Erlang BEAM VM contacting a public IP/URL that has not been seen from any beam.smp/erl.exe in the org over the baseline window. CVE-2026-8467 lets an unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary Elixir; the natural next step is :httpc.request, HTTPoison, or Finch to stage a second-stage payload or exfil data — none of which a stock Phoenix release should be doing to brand-new destinations. Rationale: Article states the injected expression runs with full Kernel imports — meaning :httpc, :inets, File, and Port modules are all usable for second-stage retrieval. Stock Phoenix release should not have beam.smp opening sockets to brand-new public destinations; leftanti baseline against 30 days of beam.smp egress is a clean way to surface only the new C2 hops without alerting on legitimate hex.pm / API integrations. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • First API integration deployment — application starts calling a new SaaS endpoint (Stripe, SendGrid, Twilio) for the first time.
  • hex.pm / DiplomaticBag / hex-cdn fetches when an Elixir release auto-pulls dependencies at start-up.
  • Cluster mesh peers (libcluster, Distributed Erlang epmd) discovering a new node added to the fleet.
  • Outbound webhook delivery from the Phoenix app to a customer-controlled URL appearing for the first time in a multi-tenant SaaS.
  • Letsencrypt ACME challenge callbacks from a custom Phoenix-driven cert manager.
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("hex.pm","repo.hex.pm","builds.hex.pm","github.com","objects.githubusercontent.com","acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org","epmd"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the BEAM process command line and PID, then pull all DNS lookups (`DnsRequest` / `DnsEvents`) from the same `aid`/`DeviceId` in the 60s preceding the connect — confirm whether the destination was resolved freshly by the same process. WHOIS the IP and check Falcon / VT for known C2 reputation. 2) Contain: NetworkIsolation on Defender or Falcon RTR if the destination is unknown/malicious; block the IP and any sibling addresses at the egress firewall. 3) Hunt: pivot on the BEAM PID to enumerate child processes (UC1 query), file writes under `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`, and the release directory, and any AsepValueUpdate events authored by the BEAM process. Search the same destination across all hosts org-wide regardless of process — multi-tenant C2 reuse is common.

    | summarize by RemoteUrl, RemoteIP;

Vulnerable phoenix_storybook artefact present in deployed Phoenix release (CVE-2026-8467 inventory) AIWeaponization Medium
Hunting query that surfaces hosts shipping a compiled phoenix_storybook in a Phoenix release directory at a version in the affected range (0.5.0 through 1.0.x). Useful for SOC/IR teams to scope blast radius after the advisory and to drive a patch wave to 1.1.0. Rationale: Article pins the affected range to phoenix_storybook >=0.5.0 <1.1.0 and explicitly names the two source files holding the vulnerable code (`extra_assigns_helpers.ex` and `component_renderer.ex`); their compiled `.beam` counterparts and the version-stamped release directory paths give a deterministic file-system fingerprint that's far cheaper than running an authenticated package-manager inventory across an Elixir fleet. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p • https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/commit/e35379dfe2ef1a71b141899e36f431017c55265d
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer laptops with the package in `~/.hex/packages/hexpm/phoenix_storybook-*` but no live Phoenix server bound to a port — true positive for inventory but not for exploit risk.
  • Build agents / CI runners that pull the dependency tree on every PR but never deploy to production.
  • Containers where the file path appears inside layered images but is masked by an overlay — same SHA reported repeatedly per container restart.
  • Demo / vendor sandboxes deliberately running the storybook on an internal-only VLAN.
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("-dev","-laptop","-buildagent","-ci-","jenkins","runner-"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the host actually exposes the storybook route (Phoenix routes file referencing `PhoenixStorybook.Router` and an open port bound to a non-loopback interface). A vulnerable artefact on disk that never serves traffic is not exploitable. 2) Contain: for internet-exposed hosts, block `/storybook` and `/live/websocket` at the WAF/reverse proxy as a stop-gap, then schedule a patch to phoenix_storybook 1.1.0. For internal hosts, require auth in front of the storybook mount. 3) Hunt: for each hit, run the UC1 BEAM-spawning-shell query and the UC2 BEAM-egress query over the prior 30 days to rule out pre-patch exploitation. Pivot on any host where the artefact appeared *and* a BEAM child shell appeared within the same week — that's the priority IR queue.

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] ServiceNow attacker IP 51.159.98.241 observed in CASB/proxy egress from corporate networks · Network connections to article IPs / domains

ServiceNow unauthenticated /api/now/related_list_edit/create access from attacker IP 51.159.98.241 AIExploitation Medium
Hunts HTTP requests to the vulnerable ServiceNow REST endpoint /api/now/related_list_edit/create, especially from the disclosed attacker IP 51.159.98.241. Targets web/proxy logs in front of ServiceNow instances or ServiceNow-shipped access logs. Rationale: Anchors on the exact vulnerable endpoint path '/api/now/related_list_edit/create' and the disclosed attacker IP 51.159.98.241 — both are unique strings from the article's Reddit-sourced admin reports. Cross-checked against the BleepingComputer bulletin which advises admins review logs for this endpoint and IP. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/servicenow-discloses-security-incident-exposing-customer-data/
ATT&CKT1190 T1213
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal ServiceNow administrators legitimately calling /api/now/related_list_edit/create from authenticated sessions after the June 5 patch
  • Pen-testers or red-team exercises probing the endpoint as part of authorised assessment
  • ServiceNow MID Server or integration accounts performing related-list maintenance
  • Security scanners (Qualys/Tenable) re-checking patch state by probing the endpoint
  • Legitimate ServiceNow REST API consumers exercising related lists in a custom application
Suppression filter
| where csUserName == "" or csUserName == "-" or cIP == "51.159.98.241"  // unauthenticated requests OR attacker IP only
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the source IP, HTTP method, response code, and any authentication header context for hits on /api/now/related_list_edit/create. Confirm whether the request was authenticated (presence of valid session/OAuth bearer) or matched 51.159.98.241; correlate against ServiceNow audit log for table reads in the same session. Step 2 — Contain: if unauthenticated or attacker-IP traffic confirmed, block 51.159.98.241 at the perimeter, force re-authentication on impacted instance, and verify the June 5, 2026 ServiceNow security update is applied (requires_authentication=true on the endpoint). Step 3 — Hunt: enumerate which sys_db_object tables were queried by the session, review exposed sys_user / sys_user_has_role / incident / sc_request tables for sensitive content, and rotate any credentials, API tokens, or secrets shared via support tickets in the exposure window.
// Defender XDR has no native ServiceNow telemetry; pivot via egress to attacker IP from corporate endpoints
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "51.159.98.241"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// Hunt across W3CIISLog / CommonSecurityLog (proxy/WAF) for the vulnerable endpoint and the attacker IP
let attackerIp = "51.159.98.241";
let vulnPath = "/api/now/related_list_edit";
(union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
     | where csUriStem has vulnPath or cIP == attackerIp
     | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csMethod, scStatus, csUserAgent, csUserName, Source="IIS"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
     | where RequestURL has vulnPath or SourceIP == attackerIp or DestinationIP == attackerIp
     | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationIP, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, SourceUserName, Source="CEF")
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ServiceNow Vulnerable Endpoint Access /api/now/related_list_edit/create
id: 8e2b6f04-7c4a-4a1e-9b9b-1f9a3b2d5c01
description: Detects HTTP requests to the ServiceNow REST endpoint /api/now/related_list_edit/create disclosed as the unauthenticated access vector in the June 2026 ServiceNow incident, or any traffic from the attacker IP 51.159.98.241.
references:

WEB

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url values(Web.src) as src values(Web.status) as status values(Web.user) as user from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url="*/api/now/related_list_edit/create*" OR Web.src="51.159.98.241" by Web.dest Web.http_method | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
ServiceNow attacker IP 51.159.98.241 observed in CASB/proxy egress from corporate networks AICommand & Control High
Hunts any HTTP/HTTPS traffic between corporate clients (via CASB, SWG, or NGFW) and 51.159.98.241 — the IP confirmed by ServiceNow admins as having issued exploit requests. Detects either compromised insider relaying through the IP, or a forensic indicator that the attacker also operated from corporate netblocks. Rationale: Single concrete IOC pivot — 51.159.98.241 — confirmed by both the BleepingComputer article and the ServiceNow admin community as the source of exploit traffic. Any hit on this IP across CASB/proxy/NGFW is high-fidelity. Bundled CloudTrail filter is included because if the same IP touched corporate AWS the call should be investigated immediately. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/servicenow-discloses-security-incident-exposing-customer-data/
ATT&CKT1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • VPN/proxy egress where 51.159.98.241 is a transit hop for non-malicious traffic (Scaleway/Online SAS netblock is shared)
  • Security researcher pivoting from corporate infra to investigate the IOC
  • Threat-intel platform connection tests verifying the IP is still live
  • Honeypot or canary infra deliberately calling the IP as part of detection validation
  • Legacy ServiceNow integration that accidentally routes through the same Scaleway hop
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: enrich 51.159.98.241 against threat-intel (Scaleway/Online SAS hosting), identify all internal hosts that connected, the process or proxy user, and the destination URL/path requested. Step 2 — Contain: block 51.159.98.241 at the perimeter and on endpoint firewalls, isolate any internal host that initiated outbound traffic, and pull a memory image if endpoint-initiated. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the same Scaleway /24 (51.159.98.0/24) for related infrastructure, review ServiceNow audit logs for table_read events from the corresponding session window, and inspect support cases for credentials or tokens that may need rotation per the BleepingComputer guidance.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "51.159.98.241"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Hits=count(), Hosts=make_set(DeviceName, 50), Processes=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 25), Users=make_set(InitiatingProcessAccountName, 25) by RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by FirstSeen asc
let attackerIp = "51.159.98.241";
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
     | where SourceIP == attackerIp or DestinationIP == attackerIp
     | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, SourceUserName, DeviceAction, Source="CEF"),
  (Syslog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
     | where SyslogMessage has attackerIp
     | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Facility, SeverityLevel, SyslogMessage, Source="Syslog"),
  (ImNetworkSession
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
     | where SrcIpAddr == attackerIp or DstIpAddr == attackerIp
     | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url, SrcUsername, Source="ASIM")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ServiceNow audit log: anonymous/guest user reading sys_db_object tables via related_list_edit AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts ServiceNow sys_audit / transaction logs for table read activity by the 'guest' or unauthenticated session identity in conjunction with the related_list_edit endpoint — the post-exploitation behaviour described where the attacker successfully queried customer instance tables. Rationale: Targets the article's confirmed post-exploitation behaviour — attackers 'successfully query the customer instance tables' — by pivoting on guest/anonymous identity reading sys_db_object tables via the disclosed endpoint. Article and BleepingComputer specifically advise customers to review sensitive ticket/record exposure, which this query surfaces. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/servicenow-discloses-security-incident-exposing-customer-data/
ATT&CKT1213 T1530
Data sourcesChange.Auditing
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Public-facing ServiceNow portal pages legitimately served to guest users (knowledge articles, public catalogs)
  • Service Catalog anonymous submission flows querying reference tables
  • ServiceNow Now Mobile or Virtual Agent unauthenticated bootstrap calls
  • Customer Service Portal widgets pre-loading data for unauthenticated visitors
  • Health-check / synthetic monitors using anonymous probe to verify availability
Suppression filter
| where not (RequestURL has_any ("/sp/","/csm/","/now/mobile") and SourceUserName == "guest")  // exclude public Service Portal / Mobile bootstrap
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: for hits, list which ServiceNow tables were queried (focus on sys_user, sys_user_has_role, incident, sc_request, sn_customerservice_case, change_request, cmdb_ci) and whether the session matched 51.159.98.241. Step 2 — Contain: confirm the June 5 2026 platform update is applied (requires_authentication=true on /api/now/related_list_edit/create), revoke any session tokens associated with anonymous reads, and snapshot affected instance for forensics. Step 3 — Hunt: enumerate records returned via correlation with sys_audit, identify exposed credentials/API tokens in incident comments and attachments, rotate them, and notify data-owners per the breach-notification process; check whether other related_list_edit subpaths (read, update) were also configured with requires_authentication=false.
// ServiceNow audit is not shipped to Defender XDR; pivot via CloudAppEvents if ServiceNow is onboarded as a CASB app
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Application has "ServiceNow"
| where (ActionType has_any ("TableRead","RecordRead","List","Query") and (AccountDisplayName has_any ("guest","anonymous") or isempty(AccountDisplayName)))
   or IPAddress == "51.159.98.241"
| project Timestamp, Application, ActionType, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, ObjectName, ObjectType, ActivityObjects, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
// Requires ServiceNow connector shipping sys_audit/transaction logs to Sentinel as CommonSecurityLog or custom table
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DeviceVendor has "ServiceNow" or DeviceProduct has "ServiceNow"
| where RequestURL has "/api/now/related_list_edit" or RequestURL has "/api/now/table/"
| where SourceUserName in~ ("guest","anonymous","") or SourceIP == "51.159.98.241"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Hits=count(), URLs=make_set(RequestURL, 50) by SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName
| where Hits > 5
| order by FirstSeen asc
@evt.name:(ServiceNow.TableRead OR ServiceNow.RecordRead OR ServiceNow.RestApiCall) (@usr.name:(guest OR anonymous) OR @network.client.ip:51.159.98.241) @http.url:*/api/now/*
APPLICATION
`servicenow_audit` (user IN ("guest","anonymous","") OR session_type="unauthenticated") (url="*/api/now/related_list_edit*" OR url="*/api/now/table/*") | stats min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime count values(tablename) as tables values(operation) as operation values(client_ip) as client_ip by user session_id | where count > 5 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("51.159.98.241") or RemoteUrl has_any ("")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["51.159.98.241"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic([""]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc
